### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

Issue Number: close #44215

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

When calculate as-of expr, calculate `now` expression by cached PD ts, the stale read ts will be more accurate, and there will also be less stale read fallback.

issue_context.title: Use estimated `now` in stale ts calculation
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

I'm running sysbench point select with 100ms staleness, and got the following error:

```
[2023/05/26 14:41:43.843 +08:00] [WARN] [session.go:2196] ["compile SQL failed"] [conn=6024217611514938189] [error="cannot set read timestamp to a future time"] [SQL="SELECT c FROM sbtest9 AS OF TIMESTAMP NOW(6) - INTERVAL 100000 MICROSECOND  WHERE id=?"]
[2023/05/26 14:41:43.843 +08:00] [INFO] [conn.go:1181] ["command dispatched failed"] [conn=6024217611514938189] [connInfo="id:6024217611514938189, addr:192.168.80.1:34542 status:10, collation:latin1_swedish_ci, user:root"] [command=Execute] [status="inTxn:0, autocommit:1"] [sql="SELECT c FROM sbtest9 AS OF TIMESTAMP NOW(6) - INTERVAL 100000 MICROSECOND  WHERE id=?"] [txn_mode=PESSIMISTIC] [timestamp=0] [err="cannot set read timestamp to a future time
github.com/pingcap/tidb/sessionctx.ValidateStaleReadTS
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/sessionctx/context.go:258
github.com/pingcap/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread.parseAndValidateAsOf
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread/processor.go:288
github.com/pingcap/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread.(*staleReadProcessor).OnSelectTable.func1
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread/processor.go:171
github.com/pingcap/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread.(*staleReadProcessor).OnExecutePreparedStmt
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/sessiontxn/staleread/processor.go:203
github.com/pingcap/tidb/planner/core.(*preprocessor).resolveExecuteStmt
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/planner/core/preprocess.go:1654
github.com/pingcap/tidb/planner/core.(*preprocessor).Enter
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/planner/core/preprocess.go:253
github.com/pingcap/tidb/parser/ast.(*ExecuteStmt).Accept
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/parser/ast/misc.go:564
github.com/pingcap/tidb/planner/core.Preprocess
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/planner/core/preprocess.go:136
github.com/pingcap/tidb/executor.(*Compiler).Compile
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/executor/compiler.go:81
github.com/pingcap/tidb/session.(*session).ExecuteStmt
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/session/session.go:2184
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*TiDBContext).ExecuteStmt
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/driver_tidb.go:252
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*clientConn).executePreparedStmtAndWriteResult
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/conn_stmt.go:277
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*clientConn).executePlanCacheStmt
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/conn_stmt.go:225
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*clientConn).handleStmtExecute
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/conn_stmt.go:217
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*clientConn).dispatch
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/conn.go:1430
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*clientConn).Run
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/conn.go:1152
github.com/pingcap/tidb/server.(*Server).onConn
	/data/tongmu/workspace/tidb/server/server.go:648
runtime.goexit
	/data/tongmu/tools/go/go/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1598
SELECT c FROM sbtest9 AS OF TIMESTAMP NOW(6) - INTERVAL 100000 MICROSECOND  WHERE id=?"]
```

TiDB first calculation the stale ts expr `TIMESTAMP NOW(6) - INTERVAL 100000 MICROSECOND`, and check it by another ts estimated by `last_pd_ts + elapsed`, here the function `NOW()` is drifted forward more than 100ms compare with `last_pd_ts + elapsed` so this error happens.

We can calculate the function `NOW()` using `last_pd_ts + elapsed`, this should be more accurate and reduce staleread miss.

review_comments: Should the `err` be returned if it's not nil?
I don't want the extra error returned by an optimization, maybe we can print it only.
Better explain more about what `cached` means here an why it's useful in certain conditions.
